title: A wall-clock refusal never mentions the WIP snapshot that holds the work
description:
SECOND occurrence. 9wo in epic 9pd, now 9fc in epic ncv.

9fc attempt 4 was refused:

    no-commits: the attempt branch carries no commit beyond the base it was
    cut from (81051f80b66d)

That sentence is TRUE and it is MISLEADING. The attempt branch had no commits; the attempt WORKTREE had 433 lines of finished-looking work across four files, and its tests pass:

    M cloudflare/src/epic-reconciler.ts        (+127)
    M cloudflare/src/run-state-store.ts        (+120)
    M cloudflare/test/epic-reconciler.test.ts  (+145)  -> 17 passed
    M internal/reconcile/closeout_ci_test.go   (+48)   -> TestTheCloseoutSeesCIPastEveryRunStateRecord ok

An operator reading 'no-commits' concludes the worker did nothing and lets the redispatch happen. It is one cleanup from being true — the worktree is removed and the work is gone. Both times it was recovered only because a person happened to look inside the worktree before cleanup ran.

The reconciler already HAS the worktree path; it reports it in every stall line. Nothing stops it from looking.

Work:
- Before refusing as no-commits, run the equivalent of git status in the attempt worktree. If the tree is dirty, that is a DIFFERENT refusal with a different name and a different repair: the work exists and is uncommitted, here is the path, here is how many files.
- Do not delete a dirty worktree on cleanup. A tree with uncommitted changes is evidence; disposing of it is the one irreversible act in an otherwise durable design.
- Consider capturing the diff into the run's durable state on this path, so recovery does not depend on an operator's reflexes.
- Test: settle an attempt whose worktree is dirty and whose branch is unmoved; assert the refusal names the dirt and the worktree survives.

Rescued this time as branch rescue/9fc-attempt-4 (3b9200f). Related: kvn (disposal ordering), and epic 9pd's retro, which records 9wo as 'its work was correct and it was refused as no-commits'.
notes:
2026-09-18 20:35 - CORRECTION — I filed this tick on a premise that is WRONG, and the correction changes what needs building.

I claimed the uncommitted work was 'one cleanup from gone' and 'recovered only because a person happened to look'. Both false. ticfac already takes a WIP snapshot at the wall-clock stop:

    .ticfac/exec/.../9fc/4/.../wip-snapshot.json
    { ref: refs/ticfac/wip/run-epic-ncv/tick-9fc/attempt-4,
      commit: e9d27e79, taken_at: 2026-09-18T17:52:56Z }

    e9d27e79  'ticfac: work-in-progress snapshot at the wall-clock stop —
               not evidence, never merged'
    4 files changed, 433 insertions(+), 7 deletions(-)

That is byte-for-byte the work I rescued by hand. The safety net exists and it WORKED. My rescue branch was redundant.

SO THE REAL DEFECT IS NARROWER AND DIFFERENT: the refusal never mentions the snapshot. An operator is told 'no-commits: the attempt branch carries no commit beyond the base' and given no hint that a commit holding an hour of work sits at a known ref. A safety net nobody is told about is barely a safety net — I had the mechanism's own output in front of me and still went and did it by hand.

Revised work:
- The no-commits refusal (and every wall-clock refusal) must NAME the WIP ref and its commit when a snapshot was taken, and say what it is: a snapshot, not evidence, never merged, here is how to look at it.
- A redispatch should be able to START from that snapshot rather than from the base, or the operator should be told plainly that it will not.
- Nothing needs building to PRESERVE the work. Delete that part of the original description.

The 'do not dispose a dirty worktree' item also needs re-examining: with a snapshot ref the worktree may be safe to remove, which makes kvn the whole of that problem.

Also recorded: the same mechanism ran for ef7 attempt 5 and its snapshot commit e66c5f03 is EMPTY. That is real evidence that ef7 produced nothing in sixty minutes, rather than an inference from a clean worktree.
acceptance_criteria: An attempt with an unmoved branch but a dirty worktree is refused with a distinct reason naming the uncommitted work and its path, the worktree is not disposed, and a test covers exactly that state
